newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: COMMERCIAL BANKS TO PROVIDE MORE INFORMATION.
newsitem.headline: COMMERCIAL BANKS TO PROVIDE MORE INFORMATION.

text.p: Lithuania's central bank said on Thursday that the country's commercial banks planned to become more transparent in a bid to make their shares more attractive on the local capital markets.

"Banks understand that they are to be transparent otherwise nobody will buy their shares on the capital markets," Vladimiras Trukshinas, the head of the central bank's information and statistics department, told a news conference.
"For the first time the country's commercial banks agreed to present 24 major indicators of their financial activity in the monthly bulletin of the Bank of Lithuania," Trukshinas said.
"Six months ago such publicity would have made a sensation and two years ago it would have been considered impossible," Trukshinas added.

Lithuania's banking sector is recovering from a crisis which erupted in late 1995 with the shock closure of two of its largest banks. A lack of transparency has been cited by analysts as one of the causes of the crisis.
It has also been cited as an obstacle to activity on the country's struggling bourse.
Trukshinas said that the statistical data can be accessed on the internet website http://www,lbank.lt.
The bank also said that the internet page will present the latest statistical information, the balance sheet and the main activities of the Bank of Lithuania.
Trukshinas said that the information will be published according to the requirements of the data standards approved by the Iinternational Monetary Fund.
